# Plugin API

`cockpitlib.plugin_api`, version 1 (the oldest version still served: 1). A plugin calls `api.require(N)` first with the version it was built for. The signatures are pinned: a change to one fails the kernel's own tests.

## ack_tickets

```python
ack_tickets(tickets) -> list
```

Acknowledge every waiting ticket-done item of these tickets, as the human's Confirm done does one: the ids.

## answer

```python
answer(card: str, text: str, pack=None) -> dict
```

The human's answer on a blocked card, with the same rules the Inbox applies.

## archive

```python
archive(card: str, reason: str, plugin: str, pack=None) -> dict
```

Archive one of a plugin's own cards: a card of a kind registered with owner=plugin. The reason is commented on it first, as the plugin; then Hermes archives it, which ends a running worker. Any other card (cockpit's own kinds, another plugin's, the human's) is refused. An archived card is left alone: no error, no second comment. {archived, was_running}. An archived card counts in no capacity and no housekeeping step brings it back.

## block

```python
block(card: str, reason: str, kind: str = '', pack=None) -> None
```

## board_cards

```python
board_cards(ticket: str = '', pack=None) -> list
```

The board's cards, or one ticket's: id, title, status, assignee, ticket, flow, kind, skills, body.

## card_thread

```python
card_thread(card: str, pack=None) -> dict
```

A card's state and what was said on it, for a plugin answering on the human's behalf: {id, title, status, block_kind, blocked_at, comments: [{author, body, at}]}, comments oldest first.

## comment

```python
comment(card: str, text: str, author: str = 'cockpit', pack=None) -> None
```

A comment on a card. On a running card Hermes hands it to the live worker.

## decide_intent

```python
decide_intent(iid: str, decision: str, note: str = '', by: str = 'plugin', pack=None) -> dict
```

A plugin's decision on a held item, on the human's behalf: confirm (endorsed as `by`; its scope's auto-publish then sends it), send_back (to its lane with `note`), or drop. The item records who decided and why.

## done_waiting

```python
done_waiting(tickets) -> list
```

The ticket-done items of these tickets still waiting for the human's ack: [{id, ticket}].

## drop_inbox_row

```python
drop_inbox_row(plugin: str, row_id: str) -> bool
```

## halted

```python
halted(ticket: str) -> str
```

'' when the ticket takes new cards; otherwise why it does not, in cockpit's words ("TASK-123 is halted ...").

## hand_over_card

```python
hand_over_card(card: str, pack=None) -> str
```

Move a card to another seat of its kind, the least busy one; the new seat, or '' when it has none. Hermes does not restart a card whose recent comments carry a PR link unless another seat takes it over, so an answered analyst card that cites PRs resumes this way.

## held_intents

```python
held_intents(tickets) -> list
```

These tickets' outbox items held for the human: what was held and why, with what a push sends.

## helper_run

```python
helper_run(name: str, verb: str, choice: str = '', background: bool = True, pack=None) -> dict
```

Run one of the pack's helpers (helpers.yaml): its dependencies first, exit 3 when one is down.

## helper_status

```python
helper_status(group: str = '', pack=None) -> dict
```

The helper groups' status rows and each helper's last run.

## inbox_row

```python
inbox_row(plugin: str, row: dict) -> str
```

A row on the human's Inbox: {id, icon, what, action_label, href, tone}. The same file contract a plugin may write itself: <records>/inbox/<plugin>/<id>.json.

## outbox_create

```python
outbox_create(ticket: str, kind: str, card: str, summary: str, payload: dict, created_by: str = 'human', pack=None) -> dict
```

An intent in the outbox, with the outbox's own checks (ticket pattern, local references, skills).

## own_tickets

```python
own_tickets(plugin: str, tickets) -> int
```

The tickets this plugin runs itself, the whole list, rewritten on each of its passes. Cockpit's watchers leave their follow-up to it: a real CI failure on one of them opens no intake card waiting for the human.

## plugin_block

```python
plugin_block(name: str, pack=None) -> dict
```

The block the bound pack gives this plugin, as the plugin's own validator returned it.

## records_root

```python
records_root() -> str
```

The workspace folder the bound pack keeps its records in.

```python
register_card_kind(name: str, title: str, flow: str = '', role: str = 'worker', owner: str = '') -> None
```

## register_kickoff_mode

```python
register_kickoff_mode(name: str, lane_kind: str, capacity_bucket: str = 'dev', title_kind: str = '', preflight=(), text: str = '', label: str = '', owner: str = '') -> None
```

## require

```python
require(version: int) -> None
```

A plugin calls this first with the API version it was built for: any version from API_MIN_SUPPORTED to API_VERSION is served; a newer one, or one this kernel no longer carries, refuses and says which side to update.

## resume_ticket

```python
resume_ticket(ticket: str) -> str
```

Lift a ticket's halt, as the ticket page's Resume does. Closed cards stay closed.

## runs

```python
runs(card: str, pack=None) -> list
```

A card's runs, oldest first: {id, status, outcome, error, summary, metadata, profile, started_at, ended_at}. The metadata carries the claims a lane put on its closing run; outcome and error are Hermes's own (a run ended for its time limit has an error starting `elapsed`).

## start_card

```python
start_card(mode: str, ticket: str, body: str = '', policy: str = 'kickoff', pack=None, prompt: str = '', idempotency_key: str = '', model_override: str = '', max_runtime_seconds: int = 0, repos=()) -> dict
```

Start a card for a kickoff mode with the Kick off page's own checks: halt, twin, capacity, the lane the pack picks, a slot, the tester's slot, the browser loan. policy="release" records the go instead of asking for it. max_runtime_seconds: Hermes ends and re-queues the card's run past this many seconds (0: no limit, as before); it is carried by the one card a mode starts, not by the per-repo rework cards a repo list makes. repos: the repos this one card works in, recorded on it (its own PRs and its repos' skills). Each is a repos.yaml name, or a short name that resolves to one (_resolve_repos); one that resolves to none or to several is refused with CockpitError and no card starts. They never fan the card out: a rework still starts one card, with its time limit; a bumps card stays keyed by its repo. Given repos, the result carries the resolved names as `repos`. Empty (the default): the card records no repos and the result is as before.

## ticket_owner

```python
ticket_owner(ticket: str) -> str
```

The plugin that runs this ticket, or ''.

## unblock

```python
unblock(card: str, pack=None) -> None
```

## wake_marker

```python
wake_marker(plugin: str) -> str
```

The file housekeeping touches when a card a plugin owns needs that plugin's attention.

## watch_prs

```python
watch_prs(plugin: str, prs) -> int
```

The PRs of the tickets this plugin runs, the whole list ([{ticket, repo, number, url, ready}]), rewritten on each pass. Cockpit's PR watch follows them like its own: the human gets a merge row once the plugin marks one ready, and a ticket's ticket-done ack once every PR of it is merged and nothing of it is open.
